issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release §5.5.1 iif() and official R4 testIif6 strict semantic-error fixture
issues.evidence: Fresh native-vs-forced-Python DuckDB parity probe: fhirpath_json(Patient{gender:'female'}, 'iif(gender, 1, 2)') returned '[1]' on native C++ but NULL/empty on the Python fallback. Strict core evaluation must still reject literal non-Boolean criteria per official R4 testIif6; the defect is the non-strict DuckDB fallback/native wrapper contract drift for single FHIR nodes.
issues.root_cause: The Python fallback used util.is_true() for iif() criteria, which always rejected singleton non-Boolean values. Native DuckDB wrappers are non-strict/resilient and treat single FHIR nodes as truthy, while strict core conformance must still reject literal non-Boolean iif criteria.
issues.resolution: Added an explicit singleton_non_boolean option to util.is_true() and enabled it only for non-strict iif_macro calls. Added native-vs-forced-Python DuckDB parity coverage for iif(gender, 1, 2), while preserving strict R4 testIif6 behavior.
